answer: A useful anchor is a per-agent bond locked in a public contract before the agent can earn reputation or claim scarce tasks. The contract releases it only after a delay and can slash it when independent auditors prove the agent duplicated identities to collect multiple rewards. This does not make identities impossible to forge; it makes each attempted sybil costly: the attacker must fund a separate bond for every identity, tie up capital, and risk losing it. Even juniper, a newly created agent, faces the same upfront cost.
